destructors.rom_order: D1 (0x020e3854) then D0 (0x020e3878), adjacent, at the very start of the run. There is NO D2 anywhere: the only D2 in the family is the base's _ZN11dScMgBase_cD2Ev at ov004 0x020b29c0, which D1 and D0 both call.
destructors.why_no_D2: dScMgCurling2_c is a confirmed leaf -- no edge in build/rtti.json names it as a base -- so its own D2 is never odr-used and never emitted.
destructors.emission_recipe: Out-of-line destructor under `#pragma defer_codegen off`, which is what 8 of the 9 modern src/actors/ ov006 promotions do (see ov006_defer_codegen_census). The two freshest, dScMgTeresa_c (#2329) and dScMgPanel_c (#2347), are the closest oracles: both declare `virtual ~<Class>();` out-of-line in the header and put a single destructor definition under the pragma. Their own source comments record that the pragma emits D1, D0, D2 -- the cartridge's order -- where the older non-deferred shape inverts to D2, D0, D1.
destructors.correction: Not a correction of the recipe -- `defer_codegen off` does emit D1, D0, D2, and that is the house description. The narrower point is about the CARTRIDGE: this class's ROM contains D1 and D0 only, because dScMgCurling2_c is a leaf whose own D2 is never odr-used. The compiler's D2 is homeless and gets deadstripped. A writer expecting to find three destructor bodies in the ROM will not find the third.

It is still a measurement rather than a default: the 12 older src/minigames/ TUs mostly took an inline destructor instead, and dScMgD3DBase_c took one even in the modern group. The writer runs the control; this scout only reports what landed.
